caption_hook: 🐱 One of the world's rarest wild cats, the Andean cat, was caught on a camera trap in Argentina + 3 more wins 👇
question: Which made you smile most: 1, 2, 3 or 4?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves cats

first_comment: Bonus: in northern Patagonia, half of the Andean cat records scientists gathered came from cats killed by ranchers. That's why the restored land near La Payunia matters. Ever seen a wild cat? 🐾

stories.headline: One of the rarest cats on Earth shows up on a camera trap
stories.summary: A remote camera near La Payunia Reserve caught the elusive Andean cat, the 'ghost of the Andes', crossing rocky slopes. It's the 3rd sighting since 2024 on land being restored for wildlife.
stories.why: It's a sign that years of habitat restoration are working for one of the most endangered cats.

stories.stat_label: proof it works on a wild reef
stories.headline: Coral 'probiotics' stopped bleaching during a heat wave
stories.summary: Scientists dosed Red Sea corals with friendly bacteria from healthy corals during a heat wave, diving 8 times in 15 days. Treated corals kept their color while the water hit 32°C.
stories.why: Even a heat-killed version worked, which could make a cheap, shelf-stable reef first-aid kit.

stories.headline: A wind turbine taller than the Eiffel Tower just went up
stories.summary: Built near Berlin, the prototype's hub sits 300 m up and its blades reach 365 m. Its developer says winds that high could make more than twice the power of today's turbines.
stories.why: Taller towers catch steadier wind, so the same site could give far more clean power.

stories.stat_label: kinds of plates, bowls and trays
stories.headline: A 2,100-year-old wreck is full of luxury Roman-era dishes
stories.summary: Off Türkiye's coast, divers working 42-55 m deep are raising thousands of plates, bowls and trays in 122 forms. The ship likely sailed from Rhosus toward Italy before a storm sank it.
stories.why: Cicero once ordered dishes from Rhosus, so this cargo matches a 2,000-year-old letter.

fun_fact: Germany's new turbine is 365 m tall, beating the 330 m Eiffel Tower by 35 m.
